speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the infant has bilious vomiting, which suggests an intestinal obstruction distal to the ampulla of Vater. Can you tell me if the baby has passed any meconium, and if so, when was the last bowel movement?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant passed any meconium stool yet, and if so, how much and when was the last passage? I also need to know if there was any delay in meconium passage beyond the first 48 hours of life.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

The bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance since birth are highly concerning for a distal intestinal obstruction, such as duodenal atresia or malrotation. An abdominal X-ray will help visualize air-fluid levels or a "double bubble" sign to narrow down the diagnosis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The provided x-ray image would show a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The physical findings are classic for Down syndrome, which has a strong association with duodenal atresia. I will request the abdominal X-ray results to confirm the diagnosis.
